definitions.explanation: The standard expression for sweating physically, whether from heat, exercise, or nervousness.

definitions.gloss: to work hard; to put in effort
definitions.explanation: Figuratively, to exert oneself or work hard at something, implying hands-on labor rather than directing from above.

examples.japanese: {暑|あつ}くて{汗|あせ}をかいた。
examples.english: I sweated because it was hot.

examples.japanese: {運動|うんどう}した{後|あと}は{気持|きも}ちよく{汗|あせ}をかける。
examples.english: After exercising, you can work up a refreshing sweat.

examples.japanese: {緊張|きんちょう}して{手|て}に{汗|あせ}をかいていた。
examples.english: I was so nervous that my palms were sweating.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}で{汗|あせ}をかかないと{成長|せいちょう}できない。
examples.english: You can't grow unless you put in the effort yourself.

examples.japanese: {上|うえ}に{立|た}つ{人|ひと}も{現場|げんば}で{汗|あせ}をかくべきだ。
examples.english: Leaders should also get their hands dirty on the ground.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{若|わか}い{頃|ころ}から{人|ひと}の{倍|ばい}{汗|あせ}をかいて{働|はたら}いてきた。
examples.english: He has worked twice as hard as others since he was young.

notes:
USAGE:
The verb かく here is a special usage meaning "to produce" (sweat). Note that this かく is written in hiragana, not with the kanji {書|か}く or {掻|か}く.

FORMS:
- {冷|ひ}や{汗|あせ}をかく: to break out in a cold sweat (from fear or a close call)
- {手|て}に{汗|あせ}をかく: to have sweaty palms (from nervousness or excitement)
- {脂汗|あぶらあせ}をかく: to break out in a greasy sweat (from pain or extreme stress)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- びっしょり{汗|あせ}をかく (to be drenched in sweat)
- {大量|たいりょう}に{汗|あせ}をかく (to sweat profusely)
- いい{汗|あせ}をかく (to work up a good sweat)
